title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 16 — QA round 4's remaining checklist findings and round 15's carried rule-6 texts
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 16 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6297142170`, PM loop round 27). It applies three sets of checklist text. First, QA round 4's remaining checklist-accuracy findings (summary `6288485402`, records #24838 and #24841, framework `307ce4c4`). Second, round 15's carried rule-6 texts (PR #24891's acceptance notes). Third, round 14's two text fixes (report `6289612504` on PR #24857).

Only checklist text changes. 27 items in 11 area files each take one `revision` bump and one `history` row, and each row names its record and finding. `RUNNER.md` takes one environment fact: two lines, the entry and its blank separator. There is no product code, test, pin or changeset text.

- Base `feb09db14a`. `origin/main` `223ae939bb` is merged in `79a13e85b7`. It touches no `docs/qa/**` path and none of the sources these edits cite.
- Every item, pin and table named below was re-read at the base before it was written. The findings that no longer held are listed under "Items left alone".
- A scripted span editor made every edit. It is round 15's editor, extended with an array-element removal and an object append, and it never re-serialises a file. For each area file it re-parses the result and asserts four things:
  - A1: the new document equals the old one with the declared ops applied.
  - A2: every other item and top-level key is value-equal.
  - A3: each edited item's changed paths lie inside its declared fields (array edits by exact index), plus `revision` and the one new history row.
  - A4: the text outside the edited items is byte-identical.
- A whole-branch check against the base agrees: 27 items changed, each with revision +1 and exactly one appended row, and no other path changed.
- The new history rows carry the placeholder ref `#PENDING-24579R16`, because a row's `ref` names this PR and the PR had no number yet. The next commit on this branch swaps in this PR's number and changes nothing else.

## What a negative is, and the 14 procedural negatives

A `negative` names a product outcome whose occurrence is the FAIL. The format documentation already defines it so: the README's item anatomy calls `negative` "the other side of every gate (deny/absence cases)". So `RUNNER.md` takes no line for it (ruling 3).

Each of #24841's 14 procedural negatives was handled one of two ways:
- **(a)** Where the procedure guards a product outcome that can be stated and measured, and that is not already a negative, the negative is rewritten into that outcome.
- **(b)** Otherwise its text moves, unchanged in substance, into `steps`. That is the schema's runner-procedure field ("how to exercise it"). There is no notes field, and `traps` is a closed vocabulary of trap names. The text is appended, so no step index shifts. Where the item already carries the same text in a procedure or notes field, the negative is removed and that carrier is named instead.

- `identity-auth.self-service-password-reset`, the `sys_email` half (#24841): no longer holds. Revision 4 (#24824) moved `requires`, `steps[1]`, `knownGaps[0]` and `acceptance[0]` to `sys_identity_email`, and the remaining `sys_email` mentions say "never sys_email". `IDENTITY_EMAIL_OBJECT` is `'sys_identity_email'` (email-log-objects.ts).

- `RUNNER.md`, a line defining a negative: not added, because the README's item anatomy already defines it.
- A fresh-install clause for #24827's order (`os migrate apply` first, then `os serve`): not added. `platform-core.v18-boot-refusals` scopes the refusal of a 17.x-shaped database and has no fresh-install clause, so it is a candidate for the anchor. The change ships in **18.1.0**: `@objectstack/cli` is in the changesets `fixed` group at 18.0.0, `.changeset/24827-migrate-apply-birth-marker.md` is `minor`, and no pending changeset is `major`. It is unpublished at the base (npm `latest` is 18.0.0).
- `records-forms.crud-roundtrip` `acceptance[6]`: its readonly half says "Score that half from the pins in `automated`, never as blocked(fixture)", under an `api` oracle, from a protocol pin over a stub engine and an engine pin. That is the rule-6 class, but it is not in this round's list, and changing a P0 clause's verdict rule is the anchor's call. Carried.
- `cli.datasource-introspect-codegen` `automated.ref` still names "acceptance[0]'s NARROWING half ONLY". Under round 15's reading no pin holds a full clause, so `automated` would go and a knownGap would replace it. The dispatch named the spelling only. Carried.
- `records-forms.record-discussion-mentions` `knownGaps[0]` / `personas[1]` (anchor comment `6290946648`, "a second signed-up user"): still present at the base, and not in this dispatch. Carried.
- Not this round, carried by the PM: the fixture gaps of #24838 and #24841, the `studio-editor` / `form-view-subforms` widening candidates, and round 12's 80 "showcase isolated" spellings.

## PM hypotheses, measured

1. "Most of the 14 are (b), fewer than five (a)." This holds: 12 are (b) and 2 are (a).
2. "`platform-core.v18-boot-refusals` is the home, and the ceremony item takes a cross-reference." This does not hold. `cli.organization-ownership-ceremony`'s title names "an 18.0 pre-release (18.0.0-next.*)" database, the moves, the webhook settlement and the boot that refuses or serves. `platform-core.v18-boot-refusals`' title names a 17.x-shaped database. So by the ruling ("the item whose scope it is") the clause sits in the ceremony item, and the boot-refusals item takes the cross-reference.

## Acceptance notes

- Some edits were located beyond the dispatch's field list, inside items it names. They were applied because they are the same rule-6 class and the item would otherwise contradict its own edit:
  - `automation.packaged-flow-subflow-disable-refusal` `negative[1]`;
  - `cli.datasource-introspect-codegen` `steps[1]` and `fixtures.knownGaps[2]`;
  - `approvals.email-action-token-door` `fixtures.knownGaps[2]`;
  - `approvals.act-door-and-admin-rescue-slate` `acceptance[1]` and `automated.ref`;
  - `integration-system.datasource-admin-lifecycle` `acceptance[3]` and `steps[8]`;
  - `records-forms.field-unique-enforcement` `automated.ref`, whose sentence quoted the old clause wording;
  - `cli.dev-boot-contract` `fixtures.requires[2]` (re-pointed to `acceptance[7]`) and `acceptance[2].verify`.
- `integration-system.datasource-admin-lifecycle` took its edit in two commits on this branch. The net diff against the base is one revision bump and one history row.
- The ceremony's `acceptance[5]` rests on #24838's measurements and on the source. Its `steps[5]`, and `cli.dev-boot-contract` `steps[9]`, were not replayed live here. `steps[9]` says so.
- A configured TTL exists: the spec declares `auth.emailAndPassword.resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn`, and auth-manager.ts forwards it to better-auth. It was not used for the expiry step. Its plumbing from a stack config was not measured, it has no liveness row, and it would still need a wait.
- `hono-approvals-act.conformance.test.ts` was read, not run, here. The objectui specs were read at the console pin `616df6598b42` with a read-only `git show`. Their verdicts at the pin are NOT MEASURED.
- `integration-system.datasource-admin-lifecycle`: two pins are not in the ref, `admin-routes-auth-guard.test.ts` (the floor) and `datasource-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` (cited by `acceptance[8].verify`). Whether either holds a whole clause at its layer was not measured.

## Gates

The derived list is `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, computed on the actual change set: 12 paths against merge base `223ae939b`, at head `e208b693b5`. It gives 13 commands. Each one ran at that head with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal`

The first run of `check:doc-formula-expressions` (at `79a13e85b7`) refused with exit 3, a prerequisite, because `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` were not built. Both were built under the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`, held 116 s, waited 0 s), and the rerun exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".

The ten new anchors all resolve, and the residual is unchanged.

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exited 0 against `223ae939bb`, and again against `19e5338cc8`, which touches no `docs/qa/**` path. No open PR touches `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`: all 16 open PRs' file lists were read in full, every page. So there was no second merge-tree to run.

There is no ablation, because no tested behaviour changed. `skip-changeset` was re-measured: `docs/qa/**` appears in none of the 73 non-private manifests' `files[]` (86 tracked `package.json` files), and the repo root is private.
